official.deadline_note: Applications are submitted twice a year, by 31 March and 31 October of the calendar year (Charles University bursary page). Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, Article 2(5), states that applications are submitted on an annual basis from 31 March to 31 October.
official.application_cycle: Current round closes 31 October 2026; the next round closes 31 March 2027. The Board convenes at least twice a year so that a meeting is held immediately after the end of the application submission period.
official.status_note: The official Charles University page (last change 1 September 2026) states applications are submitted twice a year, by 31 March and 31 October of the calendar year; the round closing 31 October 2026 is currently running.
benefits: The financial support is provided directly by Charles University.
The maximum amount of the Bursary awarded to an applicant is CZK 5,000 per month (Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, Article 4(3)).
The Bursary is paid monthly by the Finance, Human Resources and Payroll Department of the University Rectorate no later than on the 15th day of the month, including during holiday periods.
As part of the preparation for studies in the Czech language, it is possible to apply for a contribution towards living expenses.
Applicants from the Duolingo x UNHCR Access Scholars Programme are given preference by the Board and by the Rector.
eligibility: The bursary is intended for international students whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian, or other non-democratic regimes anywhere in the world.

The applicant must be directly affected by the fact that he or she comes from a country in which, according to the evaluation of generally respected humanitarian organisations, human rights and freedoms are constantly violated and in which the state exposes persons to oppression, harassment, or repression which result in discriminatory measures in relation to receiving education.
The bursary can only be awarded to a student who has been admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at one of the faculties of Charles University based on the standard admissions procedure.

An application may also be submitted by a participant in the Czech Studies lifelong learning programme of the Faculty of Arts, a participant in a programme of the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies, or an applicant for study at the University (to the dean of the faculty applied to).
Scholars of the Duolingo x UNHCR Access Scholars Programme nominated by Duolingo English Test are given preference.

The bursary may not be awarded or paid to a student who has exceeded the standard period of study or interrupted his or her study, or to a lifelong-learning participant after termination of participation.
requirements: Complete the application form available on the University website, stating the reasons (form of persecution) for which the applicant cannot complete studies in his or her own country.
Submit all documents required under Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, Article 2(3).
Duolingo x UNHCR Access Scholars Programme scholars nominated by Duolingo English Test are required to submit only the application form and the confirmation of other financial support (Article 2(4)).
Documents proving persecution may be submitted in English; a certified translation into Czech is required if they are in less commonly used foreign languages.
A bursary holder must confirm the amount of any other financial support for education by 31 October of each academic year, or submit an affirmation that he or she receives none.
documents: Completed application form (available on the University website)
Documents proving compliance with the requirement of direct affectedness (documents proving repression in the country of origin)
Transcript of study results achieved to date
Confirmation of the amount of other financial support for education, or an affirmation that the applicant receives none
Copy of diploma, if available (listed in the application form)
Certified translation into Czech for documents in less commonly used foreign languages
selection_criteria: The Board discusses and considers applications on a case-by-case basis and issues a recommendation for the Rector, including the proposed amount of the bursary.
Applicants from the Duolingo x UNHCR Access Scholars Programme are given preference by the Board and by the Rector.

The Board meets at least twice a year, immediately after the end of the application submission period, has a quorum with a majority of members, and adopts resolutions by a majority of votes of members present.
The Rector decides on awarding the bursary and on its amount on the basis of the Board's recommendation.
coverage: Monthly bursary of up to CZK 5,000 per month per applicant, paid for the standard period of study in the programme in which the student is enrolled
A contribution towards living expenses may be requested as part of the preparation for studies in the Czech language
application_method: Complete the application form and attach all required documents.

Submit the application to the Student Affairs Office of the Charles University faculty at which the student is enrolled (an applicant for study submits to the dean of the faculty applied to; participants of the Czech Studies lifelong learning programme submit to the Dean of the Faculty of Arts and participants of the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies to the director of the institute).

The faculty forwards the complete application, including all attachments, through the University's document management system (digitally), via the Dean or a Vice-Dean authorised by the Dean, to the Chair of the Vaclav Havel Bursary Board.
The dean or director refers the application, including his or her opinion, to the Board without undue delay; the Board recommends and the Rector decides on the award and its amount.
official.application_route: Submit the form and documents to the Student Affairs Office of the enrolling Faculty of Charles University; the faculty forwards the file digitally via the Dean to the Chair of the Vaclav Havel Bursary Board.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to international (foreign) students who are directly affected by coming from a country in which, according to generally respected humanitarian organisations, human rights and freedoms are constantly violated and which exposes persons to oppression, harassment or repression producing discriminatory measures in access to education.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the bursary is intended for international students; no other nationality restriction is published.
official.duration: Awarded for the standard period of study in the study programme in which the student is enrolled; for a participant in lifelong learning, for the duration of participation in the programme (Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, Article 4(2)).
official.description: The Vaclav Havel Bursary is established as a bursary designed for students of the University and participants in lifelong learning whose study is made more difficult or even impossible due to repression by totalitarian or authoritarian regimes, or regimes which are not free. Its purpose is to give an opportunity to receive education to those who were illegitimately denied it, who have been subjected to long-term pressure and repression, or who face harassment by the state and the authorities. The financial support is provided directly by Charles University.
official.program_type: University hardship bursary for students affected by repression, governed by Rector's Directive No. 56/2025 (in effect from 22 December 2025)

verification.notes: Award amount CZK 5,000 per month (maximum) taken from Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, Article 4(3), on the cuni.cz domain; deadlines, eligibility, documents, application route and the Czech-language living-expense contribution taken from the official bursary page (UKEN-2329.html, last change 1 September 2026) and the directive; the application form confirmed the attachment list. Tuition, travel and an English-test requirement are not published by the awarding body.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a hardship stipend of up to CZK 5,000 a month, not a full scholarship: the university publishes no tuition, travel or installation component, and the only extra component is a living-expense contribution tied to preparing for studies in Czech. Eligibility hinges on one thing - you must personally come from a country where human rights and freedoms are constantly violated under a repressive regime, and you must prove it. In practice you first need admission (or an active application) to a Charles University faculty, after which the faculty's Student Affairs Office shepherds your file to the bursary Board twice a year. Anyone nominated through Duolingo's UNHCR Access Scholars programme faces a far shorter form and gets formal preference.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students from countries under documented repression who have already secured (or are actively seeking) admission to a Charles University faculty, and especially Duolingo x UNHCR Access Scholars nominees.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure admission or run an active application to a Charles University faculty first; the official page states the bursary can only be awarded to a student admitted and enrolled through the standard admissions procedure.

Assemble proof of persecution in advance - the Board weighs applications case by case, and documents from humanitarian organisations or authorities in English are accepted; budget time for certified Czech translation if they originate in a less commonly used language.
Draft the personal letter to the Board as a separate attachment explaining your own situation; it is not part of the form itself.
Obtain confirmation of any other financial support you receive, or a signed affirmation that you receive none - this document is mandatory for every applicant.
Open a Czech bank account in CZK, since the application form asks for the account to which the monthly payment is made.
Submit through your faculty's Student Affairs Office in good time before the 31 March or 31 October cut-off.
common_rejection_risks: Applying without being admitted or enrolled (and without evidence of an application for study), which the official page treats as a condition for award.
Generic hardship claims without documents proving repression in the country of origin, or untranslated documents in a less commonly used foreign language.
Omitting the confirmation/affirmation about other financial support, which the directive requires of every applicant.
Leaving the standard period of study behind you - payments simply stop for students who exceed it or interrupt their studies.
Starting to receive other funding (foundation, humanitarian organisation, EU or other project) without disclosing it, which can trigger withdrawal or reduction proceedings.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, health insurance, visa and residence-permit fees, accommodation and food beyond any living-expense contribution, and any Czech-language preparation course not covered by the contribution; certified translation costs for documents in less commonly used languages are also borne by the applicant.
document_audit: Proof-of-persecution documents must be in English or accompanied by a certified Czech translation if in a less commonly used foreign language.
The personal letter to the Board, CV, and transcript of study results achieved to date are separate attachments - do not leave them until the last day.
The form asks for passport number, citizenship and a Czech CZK bank account; a missing or foreign-only account delays monthly payment.
A copy of the diploma, if available, should be attached even though it is not among the directive's mandatory items.
Duolingo x UNHCR Access Scholars nominees should file only the form plus the financial-support confirmation as the directive permits.
alerts: Only two windows per year (31 March and 31 October); the Board convenes immediately after each, so a missed 31 October can cost roughly six months of support.
Rector's Directive No. 56/2025 replaced No. 24/2022 with effect from 22 December 2025 - check you are reading the current rules, especially the new CZK 5,000 monthly maximum.
Every academic year, holders must reconfirm other funding by 31 October; silence or an inaccurate affirmation risks withdrawal proceedings.
Do not budget this as a tuition waiver; the published documents only speak of a monthly stipend and a Czech-language living-expense contribution.
The award follows the standard study period - if you plan to repeat or take a long break, ask the faculty how it will be handled before relying on the payment.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You file the form and attachments with your faculty's Student Affairs Office, the Dean forwards the file digitally with an opinion to the Chair of the Vaclav Havel Bursary Board, the Board meets immediately after each window and recommends an amount, and the Rector issues the final decision.
